instructions.text: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and season lightly with salt.
Melt half the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add the garam masala, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add the tomato paste and canned tomatoes. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the chicken and simmer until cooked through.
Stir in the remaining butter and the cream. Simmer gently for 2 more minutes and adjust salt to taste.
Serve hot over basmati rice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder, and toast for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes and simmer until slightly reduced.
Add the chickpeas with their liquid. Simmer until thickened, mashing a few chickpeas against the pot to thicken the sauce.
Season with salt to taste and top with fresh cilantro.
Serve hot over basmati rice.
Thaw the spinach and roughly puree it in a blender with a splash of water.
Cut the paneer into cubes. Pan-fry in a little oil until lightly golden on each side, then set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining oil and toast the cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the pureed spinach and garam masala. Simmer gently.
Fold in the cream and paneer, and warm through without boiling.
Season with salt and serve hot with naan.
Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear.
Simmer the lentils with the turmeric in enough water to cover by an inch, until soft.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard and cumin seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the onion and cook until golden, then the garlic and ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped tomato and cook until it breaks down.
Pour the onion-tomato mixture into the cooked lentils and stir to combine. Season with salt.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot over basmati rice.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear and set aside to drain.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Add the bay leaf and cumin seeds and cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden, then add the garlic and ginger.
Add the carrots, garam masala, and cardamom, and stir to coat.
Add the rice and enough water to cook it through, along with the peas. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat until the rice is tender.
Let the rice rest off the heat, covered, for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with a dollop of yogurt.
Season the chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and half the oregano.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken over medium-high heat until cooked through and lightly charred.
Rest the chicken for a few minutes, then slice.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into large chunks, and thinly slice the red onion.
Toss the vegetables and olives with the olive oil, lemon juice, and remaining oregano.
Top the salad with crumbled feta and the sliced chicken. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat the olive oil in a pot. Add the onion and cook until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika, and cook until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas with their liquid. Simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir in the spinach and cook until just wilted.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and season with salt to taste.
Serve warm with pita bread.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Slice the zucchini and toss with a little olive oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan. Place the salmon fillets alongside.
Mix the minced garlic with the remaining olive oil and lemon juice, and spoon over the salmon.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and the zucchini is tender.
Meanwhile, pour boiling water or hot broth over the couscous, cover, and let it steam.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and stir in the chopped parsley.
Serve the salmon and zucchini over the couscous with a lemon wedge.

title: Falafel-Style Chickpea Patties with Tahini Sauce

instructions.text: Pat the chickpeas dry and pulse them in a food processor with the garlic, cumin, coriander, and parsley until coarsely ground — not pureed.
Mix in the flour until the mixture holds together, then shape into small patties.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Pan-fry the patties until golden and crisp on both sides.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice and a splash of water until smooth and pourable, seasoning with salt.
Serve the patties warm in pita with tahini sauce drizzled over top.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika, and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the canned tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Crumble feta over top and serve straight from the pan with pita bread.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into thin strips and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the chicken until golden and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the garlic until fragrant, then add the cream and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the parmesan until the sauce is smooth, then return the chicken to the pan.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce and garnish with parsley and black pepper.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Drain excess fat, then stir in the chili powder, cumin, and a splash of water. Simmer until thickened.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or in the oven.
Dice the tomato and red onion, and shred the lettuce.
Assemble the tacos with beef, cheddar, tomato, onion, lettuce, and cilantro.
Finish with a squeeze of lime and a dollop of sour cream.
Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and bell pepper, and cook until softened.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, and paprika, and toast for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes and black beans with their liquid. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Season with salt to taste and serve topped with shredded cheddar.
Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F).
Cut the potatoes and carrots into similarly sized chunks.
Toss the chicken, potatoes, and carrots with olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast until the chicken and potatoes are almost cooked through.
Add the broccoli florets to the pan and toss with the remaining oil.
Return to the oven and roast until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Divide the ground beef into four patties, season with salt and pepper, and press a shallow dimple in the center of each.
Cook the bacon in a pan until crisp, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the patties over medium-high heat to your desired doneness, topping with cheddar in the last minute.
Toast the buns lightly in the same pan.
Slice the tomato and red onion.
Assemble the burgers with mustard, lettuce, tomato, onion, and bacon.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chili and cook for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander and salt, then the tomatoes. Cook, stirring, until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower, toss to coat, splash in 60 ml water, cover and cook on medium-low until tender, stirring every few minutes.
Uncover, sprinkle over the garam masala and cook a few minutes more to dry off any liquid. Finish with cilantro.
Whisk the eggs with the salt in a bowl.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the onion and green chili and cook until the onion is soft.
Add the tomato, turmeric and chili powder and cook until the tomato softens.
Lower the heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set but still soft.
Fold through the cilantro and serve with warm naan.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds, then the onion, and cook until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground chicken and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the coriander, turmeric, chili powder and salt, then the tomatoes.
Cover and simmer until the tomatoes have cooked down into the meat.
Add the peas and garam masala and cook until the peas are hot.
Scatter with cilantro and serve with basmati rice.
Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin and salt until smooth, adding a spoonful or two of the reserved chickpea liquid to loosen.
Spread a thick layer of hummus over each tortilla, leaving a border.
Layer on the lettuce, cucumber, carrot and tomato.
Roll up tightly, tucking in the sides, and cut in half to serve. Leftover hummus keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
Mix the juice of half the lemon with 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 cloves of garlic (grated), the oregano, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken in it.
For the tzatziki, stir the grated cucumber, remaining garlic, remaining lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil into the Greek yogurt. Season with a pinch of salt.
Cook the chicken in a hot grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the pitas in the pan.
Fill each pita with chicken, tomato, red onion and a generous spoonful of tzatziki.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).

Put the tomatoes and garlic in a baking dish, set the feta block in the middle, drizzle everything with the olive oil and season with the salt, pepper and chili flakes. Bake until the tomatoes burst and the feta is soft.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.
Mash the feta and tomatoes together in the dish, adding a splash of pasta water to make a creamy sauce.
Toss in the pasta, and the spinach if using, until coated. Finish with torn basil.

ingredients.note: thinned with lemon and water, to drizzle

instructions.text: Mix half the yogurt with the juice of half the lemon, the garlic, cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and olive oil. Coat the chicken thighs and let them sit while the rice cooks.
Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, over low heat.
Cook the chicken in a hot skillet over medium-high heat until charred and cooked through, turning once.
Rest the chicken, then slice it.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, lettuce, cucumber and tomato. Top with the remaining yogurt and a drizzle of tahini.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Toss the sweet potato with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin and salt and roast on a sheet pan until tender and browned at the edges.
Warm the black beans in a small pot with a splash of water and a squeeze of lime.
Char the tortillas briefly in a dry pan or over a gas flame.
Fill the tortillas with sweet potato and beans, then top with avocado, red onion, cilantro, a squeeze of lime and sour cream if you like.

ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the pan

instructions.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, eggs and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined — a few lumps are fine.
Heat a lightly buttered pan over medium heat. Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake and cook until bubbles appear on top.
Flip and cook until golden underneath.
Keep warm while you cook the rest. Serve with honey.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the bell pepper until softened, then add the spinach and green onion and cook until wilted. Set the vegetables aside.
Melt the rest of the butter, pour in half the eggs and cook, pulling the set edges into the middle, until almost set.
Spoon half the vegetables and cheese over one side, fold, and slide onto a plate.
Repeat with the remaining eggs and filling for a second omelette. Cut each in half to serve four.
Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, over low heat.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through. Remove.
Add the remaining oil, then the broccoli, carrot and bell pepper. Stir-fry until crisp-tender, adding a splash of water if the pan is dry.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss until glossy.
Serve over rice, scattered with green onion.
Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, over low heat.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, until golden and crisp on most sides. Remove.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar and sesame oil together.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the broccoli, bell pepper and carrot until crisp-tender.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, return the tofu, pour over the sauce and toss to coat.
Serve over rice with green onion.
Cook the pasta in boiling water until just tender. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger, loosening with the reserved water until pourable.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, cucumber, carrot and most of the green onion.
Top with the remaining green onion and chili flakes. Good cold the next day for lunch.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until softened.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the broth and add the bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer, add the whole chicken breasts and poach gently until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and discard the bay leaves.
Add the pasta to the pot and simmer until tender.
Return the chicken, season with salt and pepper, and stir in the parsley.

ingredients.note: cooked and cooled — day-old is best

instructions.text: If you don't have leftover rice, cook it with 3 cups of water, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry before frying.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the shrimp until pink, then remove.
Scramble the eggs in the wok until just set, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, the carrot, peas and corn, and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the garlic.
Add the rice and fry, pressing it against the hot wok, until heated through and slightly crisp.
Return the shrimp and egg, add the soy sauce, sesame oil and most of the green onion, and toss. Top with the rest of the green onion.
Blend the green onions, jalapeños, garlic, ginger, lime juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, cinnamon, pepper, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and marinate as long as you can.
Roast at 220°C (425°F) until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the package directions.
Serve the chicken over rice with lime wedges.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Dice the onion and bell pepper and cook in the oil until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook until fragrant.
Add the beans with their liquid and the bay leaves, and simmer until thick.
Squeeze in the lime juice and serve the beans over the rice.
Dice the potatoes small and fry in the oil until golden.
Add the beef, onion, bell pepper, and garlic and cook until the beef is browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, sliced olives, cumin, and oregano.
Simmer until thick and the potatoes are tender.
Serve with rice.
Season the chicken and brown it in the oil, then set aside.
Cook the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in the same pot until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, turmeric, cumin, and rice until the rice is coated.
Add the broth and return the chicken to the pot. Cover and simmer until the rice is tender.
Stir in the peas and olives, cover for a few minutes, and top with cilantro.
Cut the chicken, potatoes, and carrots into chunks.
Toast the turmeric, cumin, coriander, and pepper in the oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, and jalapeño and stir until the chicken is coated and lightly browned.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and 480 ml water. Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Top with green onion and serve with rice.
Dice the onion and potatoes.
Cook the onion, garlic, and chili in the oil until soft.
Add the spices with a splash of water and fry until the paste darkens.
Add the potatoes, drained chickpeas, and 480 ml water and simmer until the potatoes break down and thicken the curry.
Finish with cilantro.
Season the chicken with lime juice, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil with the brown sugar until it caramelizes, then brown the chicken in it.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and tomato paste and stir for a few minutes.
Add the cubed potatoes, olives, and 360 ml water. Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Top with cilantro and serve with rice or bread.
Shred the cabbage and slice the carrots, onion, and bell pepper thinly.
Melt the butter and cook the onion, garlic, and jalapeño until soft.
Add the cabbage, carrots, bell pepper, and 60 ml water.
Cover and steam until tender but still bright.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Cook the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and jalapeño in the oil until soft.
Add the spices and tomatoes and cook into a thick sauce.
Add the shrimp and a splash of water and simmer until pink.
Finish with lime juice and serve over rice.
Rub the butter into the flour, 1 tsp turmeric, and a pinch of salt, then add cold water until a dough forms. Chill.
Brown the beef with the onion, green onion, jalapeño, chili powder, and remaining turmeric.
Add 120 ml water and the breadcrumbs and simmer until thick, then cool.
Roll the dough thin, cut into rounds, fill, fold, and crimp the edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C (400°F) until golden.
Dice the onion, bell pepper, and carrot and cook in the oil until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook until fragrant.
Add the beans and broth and simmer.
Blend about half the soup to thicken it.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro.
Thinly slice the onion, bell pepper, carrot, and jalapeño.
Simmer the vegetables in the vinegar with the sugar, pepper, and a pinch of salt until just softened.
Season the salmon and pan-fry in the oil until crisp and cooked through.
Spoon the hot pickled vegetables and their liquid over the salmon to serve.
Chop the onion, tomatoes, and green onions.
Cook the onion, garlic, and jalapeño in the butter until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Add the spinach with a splash of water, cover, and cook until tender.
Season and serve as a side or with rice.

title: Caribbean Sweet Potato and Black Bean Curry

instructions.text: Peel and cube the sweet potatoes and dice the onion and bell pepper.
Cook the onion, pepper, garlic, and ginger in the oil until soft.
Add the turmeric and cumin and stir for a minute.
Add the sweet potatoes, tomatoes, and 240 ml water and simmer until tender.
Stir in the beans and spinach and cook until hot. Finish with lime juice.
Simmer the chicken breasts in salted water with the bay leaves until cooked through, then shred.
Slice the onion and bell peppers into strips and cook in the oil until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, and tomato paste and cook for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, olives, shredded chicken, and a splash of the cooking water, and simmer until thick.
Serve with rice or black beans.
Blend the green onions, jalapeño, garlic, lime juice, brown sugar, cinnamon, soy sauce, and oil.
Toss the shrimp in the marinade.
Thread the shrimp and chunks of bell pepper onto skewers.
Grill or broil until the shrimp are pink and lightly charred.
Serve with lime wedges.
Season the chicken with soy sauce, garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil with the brown sugar until it turns dark amber, then brown the chicken in it.
Add the onion, bell pepper, tomatoes, and carrots and stir to coat.
Add 360 ml water, cover, and simmer until the chicken is tender and the gravy is rich.
Top with green onion and serve with rice.
Whisk the lime juice, crushed garlic, cumin, oregano, and olive oil into a mojo marinade.
Marinate the chicken with the sliced onion.
Roast at 220°C (425°F) with the onions until golden and cooked through.
Spoon the pan juices over the chicken and top with cilantro.
Peel and chop the sweet potatoes, onion, and carrot.
Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger in the oil until soft.
Add the sweet potatoes, carrot, cinnamon, and broth and simmer until very tender.
Blend until smooth and finish with lime juice.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Cook the onion and garlic in half the oil until soft, then add the tomatoes and simmer into a sauce.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the edges are crisp.
Serve the rice topped with the tomato sauce and fried eggs.

title: Fry Bake with Spiced Scrambled Eggs

instructions.text: Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt, then add water to make a soft dough. Rest.
Divide into small balls, flatten, and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden.
Dice the tomato, onion, and jalapeño and cook until soft.
Add the beaten eggs and scramble until just set.
Split the warm bakes and fill with the eggs.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and cut the tomatoes into wedges.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil until just set, then set aside.
Cook the tomatoes in the remaining oil until they soften into a sauce.
Add the sugar and soy sauce, return the eggs, and fold together.
Top with green onion and serve with rice.
Simmer the broth with the ginger and corn.
Whisk the flour with 3 tbsp cold water and stir into the broth to thicken slightly.
Slowly pour in the beaten eggs while stirring the soup in one direction to make ribbons.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil and top with green onion.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Cut the tofu into cubes and blanch in salted water to firm up.
Brown the beef in the oil, then add the garlic, ginger, chili powder, and pepper flakes.
Add the broth and soy sauce, then gently slide in the tofu and simmer.
Thicken with the flour whisked into a little cold water and simmer until glossy.
Top with green onion and serve over rice.
Cut the broccoli into florets.
Stir-fry the garlic in the oil until fragrant.
Add the broccoli and a splash of water, cover, and steam until bright green.
Uncover, add the soy sauce and sugar, and toss until glossy.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Cut the chicken into chunks, dip in beaten egg, and toss in flour.
Shallow-fry until golden and cooked through, then drain.
Stir-fry the pepper and onion chunks in a little oil until crisp-tender.
Add the tomato paste, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, and 60 ml water and simmer until syrupy.
Toss in the chicken and serve over rice.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Slice the chicken, dip in beaten egg, and coat in flour.
Shallow-fry until golden and cooked through.
Simmer the lemon zest and juice, honey, soy sauce, and 60 ml water until slightly thick.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and top with green onion.
Cook the spaghetti until just tender, drain, and toss with the sesame oil.
Slice the chicken and shred the cabbage and carrot.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil until cooked.
Add the vegetables and stir-fry until crisp-tender.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, and sugar and toss until slightly crisp in spots. Finish with green onion.
Cook the pasta until al dente and drain.
Slice the mushrooms, pepper, and carrot.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger, and vegetables in the oil until tender.
Add the spinach, noodles, soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil and toss until coated and hot.
Mix the flour with 180 ml boiling water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough. Rest, covered.
Divide the dough into four, roll each thin, brush with sesame oil, and scatter with sliced green onion.
Roll each up like a rope, coil into a snail, and roll flat again.
Pan-fry in the oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Cut into wedges and serve with soy sauce mixed with rice vinegar.
Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife, cut into chunks, and salt them.
Drain the liquid.
Toss with the garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and pepper flakes.
Cook the noodles, adding the spinach for the last 30 seconds, then drain.
Brown the beef in the oil with 1 tbsp soy sauce until crisp.
Whisk the tahini, remaining soy sauce, chili powder, pepper flakes, sesame oil, vinegar, sugar, and garlic with a splash of hot water.
Divide the sauce among bowls, add the noodles and spinach, and top with the beef and green onion.
Toss everything together before eating.
Simmer the broth with the sliced mushrooms and cubed tofu.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, and pepper.
Whisk the flour with a little cold water and stir in to thicken.
Drizzle in the beaten eggs while stirring to form ribbons.
Finish with sesame oil and green onion.
Dice the carrot and slice the green onions.
Scramble the eggs in the oil into small pieces.
Add the carrot and peas and stir-fry for a minute.
Add the rice and stir-fry until hot and separate.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil and fold in the green onion.
Cook the rice and steam the broccoli.
Cut the chicken into chunks, dip in egg, and coat in flour.
Fry until crisp and cooked through, then drain.
Cook the garlic, ginger, and pepper flakes in a little oil, then add the soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, tomato paste, and 60 ml water.
Simmer until syrupy, then toss in the chicken.
Serve with rice and broccoli.
Slice the chicken and shred the cabbage, carrot, and mushrooms.
Scramble the eggs and set aside.
Stir-fry the chicken until cooked, then add the vegetables until wilted.
Add 2 tbsp soy sauce and the eggs and toss.
Mix the honey, tomato paste, and remaining soy sauce into a quick hoisin-style sauce.
Serve in warm tortillas with the sauce and green onion.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Scatter half the ginger matchsticks over the salmon and steam until just cooked.
Top with the remaining ginger and the shredded green onion.
Heat the oil until smoking and pour it over the salmon so the aromatics sizzle.
Drizzle with soy sauce and serve with rice.
Rinse the rice and simmer with the broth, ginger, and whole chicken thighs, stirring often.
Remove the chicken, shred it, and return it to the pot.
Simmer until the rice has broken down into a creamy porridge, adding water if needed.
Serve with soy sauce, sesame oil, and green onion.
Cut the zucchini, peppers, onion, and fresh tomatoes into chunks.
Cook the onion and peppers in the oil until soft.
Add the zucchini and garlic and cook for a few minutes.
Add the fresh and canned tomatoes and oregano and simmer gently until everything is tender and jammy.
Stir in torn basil and serve warm or at room temperature.
Rub the butter into the flour and a pinch of salt, add 3–4 tbsp ice water, and chill the dough.
Roll out the dough, line a tart pan, and blind-bake at 200°C (400°F) until pale golden.
Fry the diced bacon and sliced onion until the bacon is crisp.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, salt, and pepper.
Scatter the bacon, onion, and cheese in the crust and pour in the custard.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) until just set in the center.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt until completely smooth.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat until foaming.
Add the eggs and stir quickly with a spatula while shaking the pan until softly set.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and green onion, then roll the omelette onto a plate seam-side down.
Cook the bacon until crisp.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Stir in half the cheese.
Spread the bread with mustard and make sandwiches with the bacon and some cheese.
Spread the cheese sauce on top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) until bubbling and golden.
Fry the diced bacon until crisp, then set aside.
Brown the seasoned chicken in the bacon fat, then set aside.
Cook the onion, carrots, and mushrooms until browned.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and flour, then add the broth and bay leaves.
Return the chicken and bacon, cover, and simmer until tender.
Top with parsley.
Season the chicken and cook gently in the butter without browning much, then set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot, and mushrooms until soft.
Stir in the flour, then the broth, and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the cream and lemon juice and simmer until silky. Top with parsley.
Slice the onions thinly and cook slowly in the butter, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Stir in the flour, then add the broth and bay leaf and simmer.
Toast the bread.
Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, float a toast on each, and cover with the cheeses.
Broil until bubbling and browned.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a baking dish.
Peel and slice the potatoes very thinly.
Warm the cream, milk, crushed garlic, salt, and pepper.
Layer the potatoes in the dish and pour the cream over them, then top with parmesan.
Bake until tender and golden on top.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, sugar, half the melted butter, and a pinch of salt into a thin batter. Rest.
Brush a nonstick pan with butter and pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling to cover.
Cook until the edges lift, then flip and cook the other side.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve with a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of sugar.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, and cinnamon.
Soak each slice of bread in the custard for a few seconds per side.
Cook in butter over medium heat until golden on both sides.
Serve drizzled with honey.
Boil the potatoes until tender and hard-boil the eggs.
Roast the salmon at 200°C (400°F) until it flakes.
Whisk the olive oil, mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Arrange the lettuce, halved potatoes, eggs, tomatoes, olives, sliced onion, and flaked salmon on plates.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette.
Season the chicken and sear in the oil and butter until cooked through, then set aside.
Cook the garlic briefly, then add the broth and scrape up the browned bits.

Rest covered, then fluff with a fork.
Char the corn in a hot dry skillet until blistered in spots.
Stir in the butter.
Mix the sour cream with the lime juice.
Spoon the corn into cups and top with the lime cream, parmesan, chili powder, and cilantro.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and a good pinch of salt.
Finely dice the red onion, tomato, and jalapeño and chop the cilantro.
Fold everything together and serve with tortilla chips or vegetables.
Cut the tortillas into strips and fry in the oil until crisp.
Add the diced onion, jalapeño, and tomato and cook until soft.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble gently until just set.
Fold in the cheese and serve.
Dice the potatoes and carrots small.
Brown the beef with the onion and garlic in the oil.
Add the potatoes, carrots, tomatoes, cumin, and 120 ml water.
Cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the peas and serve with warm tortillas.
Brown the beef with the chili powder, cumin, and a splash of water.
Chop the lettuce and tomatoes and rinse the beans.
Thin the sour cream with lime juice for a dressing.
Pile the lettuce with beef, beans, tomatoes, cheese, and avocado, and drizzle with the dressing.
Toss the shrimp with chili powder, garlic powder, salt, and the juice of one lime.
Shred the cabbage and toss with a squeeze of lime.
Mix the sour cream with the remaining lime juice.
Sear the shrimp in the oil until pink.
Fill the warm tortillas with slaw, shrimp, lime cream, and cilantro.
Cook the onion, garlic, and jalapeño in the oil until soft.
Add the cumin, tomatoes, beans, and broth and simmer.
Blend until mostly smooth.
Finish with lime juice and serve with sour cream and cilantro.
Dice the zucchini, tomatoes, onion, and jalapeño.
Cook the onion, garlic, and jalapeño in the oil until soft.
Add the zucchini and corn and cook until just tender.
Add the tomatoes and cook until softened.
Top with cheese and let it melt before serving.
Toast the broken noodles in the oil, stirring, until golden.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, and garlic until smooth.
Add the tomato mixture to the noodles and cook for a few minutes.
Add the broth and simmer until the noodles are tender.
Serve with lime and cilantro.
Dice the potatoes and fry in the oil until crisp and tender.
Cook the diced bacon, pepper, and onion until the bacon is crisp.
Scramble the eggs until just set.
Fill the tortillas with potatoes, bacon mixture, eggs, and cheese, and roll up tightly.
Toast seam-side down in a dry pan until golden.
Dice the onion, carrot, and potato and cook in the oil until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, and paprika.
Add the rinsed lentils and broth and simmer until everything is very soft.
Blend until smooth.
Serve with lemon wedges and torn mint.

title: Turkish Pasta with Yogurt and Spiced Beef

instructions.text: Cook the pasta until al dente.
Brown the beef with the diced onion, then stir in the tomato paste.
Mix the yogurt with the grated garlic and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter with the paprika and pepper flakes until sizzling.
Spread the garlic yogurt on plates, top with pasta and beef, drizzle with the spiced butter, and add mint.
Stir the yogurt with the grated garlic and a pinch of salt and let it come to room temperature.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water.
Melt the butter with the paprika and pepper flakes until foaming.
Spread the yogurt on plates, top with the eggs, and spoon the spiced butter over.
Serve with toasted bread.
Tear the pita into pieces, toss with 1 tbsp oil, and toast until crisp.
Chop the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, and onion.
Whisk the lemon juice, remaining oil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Toss the salad, herbs, and dressing, and fold in the pita chips just before serving.
Mix the beef, grated onion, chopped parsley, garlic, and spices with salt.
Shape into long ovals around skewers or into small logs.
Grill or pan-fry, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Stir the grated cucumber into the yogurt with a pinch of salt.
Serve the kofta in warm pita with the yogurt sauce.
Drain the chickpeas, saving some of the liquid.
Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and a pinch of salt until very smooth, adding liquid as needed.
Spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and dust with paprika.
Serve with carrot and cucumber sticks.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, tomato paste, paprika, oregano, oil, and salt.
Cut the chicken into cubes and marinate.
Thread onto skewers with chunks of pepper and onion.
Grill or broil, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Toast the broken pasta in the butter until deep golden.
Add the rice and stir to coat, then add the broth and a pinch of salt.
Cover and simmer on low until tender.
Rest covered, then fluff with a fork.
Brown the seasoned chicken in the oil, then set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic until soft, then add the spices, tomatoes, and tomato paste.
Return the chicken, add the broth, and simmer.
Add the rinsed rice and grated carrot, cover, and cook until the rice is tender.
Top with toasted almonds.
Roast the cauliflower florets and sliced potatoes with half the oil at 220°C (425°F) until golden.
Brown the chicken with the onion and spices in the remaining oil, then add the broth and simmer.
Layer the chicken, then the vegetables, then the rinsed rice in a deep pot. Strain the broth over to cover.
Cover and cook on low until the rice is tender.
Rest, then flip the pot onto a platter and top with toasted almonds.
Season the chicken with paprika, cumin, cinnamon, lemon juice, and salt and roast at 200°C (400°F).
Slowly cook the sliced onions in the olive oil with a pinch of the spices until soft and sweet.
Shred the chicken and fold it into the onions.
Spread over the pitas, scatter with toasted almonds, and warm in the oven until crisp at the edges.
Finely chop the herbs and green onions and roughly chop the walnuts.
Beat the eggs with the turmeric, baking powder, salt, and pepper, then fold in the herbs and nuts.
Pour into a hot oiled skillet, cover, and cook on low until set underneath.
Flip or finish under the broiler until set.
Cut into wedges and serve with yogurt.
Cook the diced pepper and onion in the oil until soft.
Add the grated or chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Stir in the beaten eggs and cook gently until softly set.
Top with pepper flakes and feta and serve with bread.

title: Stuffed Zucchini with Beef and Rice

instructions.text: Halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the centers, keeping the flesh.
Mix the beef, rinsed rice, diced onion, chopped zucchini flesh, spices, mint, and salt.
Fill the zucchini and set them in a baking dish.
Pour the tomatoes and 120 ml water around them, cover, and bake at 190°C (375°F).
Uncover and bake until the tops brown.
Cook the diced onion in the butter until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika.
Add the rinsed lentils, rice, and broth and simmer until thick and soft.
Stir in chopped mint and serve with lemon.
Drain the chickpeas and pat very dry.
Toss with the oil and roast at 220°C (425°F), shaking once, until crisp.
Toss with the oregano, cumin, paprika, lemon zest, and salt while hot.
Cool before storing.
Cook the pasta until just al dente and drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk.
Simmer until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the cheese and mustard until smooth.
Fold in the pasta and season with salt and pepper.
Finely dice the onion and soak the breadcrumbs in the milk.
Mix the beef, onion, breadcrumbs, eggs, garlic, salt, and pepper without overworking.
Shape into a loaf on a lined pan.
Stir the tomato paste, brown sugar, mustard, and a splash of water into a glaze and spread on top.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) until cooked through, then rest before slicing.
Brown the beef with the diced onion and pepper.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, brown sugar, mustard, and chili powder.
Simmer until thick.
Pile onto toasted buns.
Dice the chicken, onion, carrots, and celery.
Cook the vegetables and chicken in 2 tbsp butter until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in 3 tbsp of the flour, then the broth and half the milk, and simmer until thick. Add the peas.
Rub the remaining butter into the remaining flour, the baking powder, and salt, then stir in the remaining milk for a biscuit dough.
Drop spoonfuls over the filling and bake at 200°C (400°F) until golden.
Cook the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp butter until soft.
Add the tomatoes and broth and simmer.
Blend until smooth and stir in the cream.
Butter the bread, fill with cheese, and toast in a skillet until golden and melted.
Serve the sandwiches with the soup.
Season the chicken and sear in the oil until cooked through, then slice.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, half the parmesan, salt, and pepper into a dressing.
Chop the lettuce and toss with the dressing and remaining parmesan.
Fill the tortillas with the salad and chicken and roll up.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Pound or finely chop the garlic and chilies.
Stir-fry the garlic and chilies in the oil until fragrant, then add the chicken and cook until done.
Add the soy sauce and brown sugar and toss, then fold in the basil until wilted.
Fry the eggs until crispy at the edges.
Serve the chicken over rice, topped with a fried egg.
Slice the chicken into strips and marinate with the turmeric, coriander, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and brown sugar.
Thread onto skewers and grill or broil until charred and cooked through.
Whisk the peanut butter, remaining soy sauce, lime juice, pepper flakes, garlic, and hot water into a dipping sauce.
Serve the skewers with the sauce and sliced cucumber.
Toast the raw rice in a dry pan until golden, then grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the chicken with a splash of water, breaking it up, until just done.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice, soy sauce, pepper flakes, sliced red onion, and green onion.
Fold in the mint, cilantro, and toasted rice powder.
Serve in lettuce cups.
Slice the chicken thinly and cut the onion and tomato into wedges.
Stir-fry the garlic and chicken in the oil until the chicken is cooked.
Push aside, scramble the eggs, then add the onion and rice and stir-fry until hot.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, and tomato and toss.
Serve with lime wedges, cucumber slices, and green onion.
Thinly slice the cucumbers and red onion.
Stir the vinegar, sugar, pepper flakes, and a pinch of salt until dissolved.
Toss the vegetables in the dressing and let sit for a few minutes.
Top with cilantro and chopped almonds.
Cook the pasta, saving some cooking water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, honey, garlic, and ginger with hot water into a sauce.
Slice the chicken and stir-fry in the oil until cooked.
Add the carrot and pepper strips and cook until crisp-tender.
Toss with the noodles and sauce and top with cilantro.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Beat the eggs hard with the soy sauce and a squeeze of lime until frothy.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot.
Pour in the eggs from a height so they puff up, then flip once the bottom is crisp and golden.
Drain and serve over rice with green onion.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Pound the garlic, pepper, and cilantro stems into a paste.
Slice the chicken and toss with the paste and soy sauce.
Stir-fry in the oil until golden and cooked through, then add the brown sugar to glaze.
Serve over rice with cucumber.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Simmer the honey, vinegar, pepper flakes, garlic, and a pinch of salt into a sweet chili glaze.
Place the salmon and broccoli on a sheet pan and brush the salmon with half the glaze.
Roast at 220°C (425°F) until the salmon flakes.
Brush with the remaining glaze and serve with lime and rice.
Brown the beef, breaking it up, and drain any fat.
Stir in the lime juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, and pepper flakes.
Fold in the sliced red onion, mint, and basil.
Serve in lettuce cups with shredded carrot.

title: Crispy Tofu with Thai Peanut Sauce

instructions.text: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Press and cube the tofu, toss in flour, and pan-fry in the oil until golden.
Steam the broccoli florets until bright green.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, and honey with hot water into a sauce.
Serve the tofu and broccoli over rice with the sauce.
Simmer the broth with the ginger, garlic, and bruised chilies to infuse.
Add the sliced mushrooms and tomato wedges and simmer.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice and soy sauce and taste for a balance of sour and salty.
Top with cilantro.
Cook the noodles until just tender, drain, and toss with a little oil.
Slice the chicken and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Stir-fry the garlic and chicken in a very hot pan until cooked.
Add the broccoli and a splash of water and cook until crisp-tender.
Push aside, scramble the eggs, then add the noodles, soy sauce, and sugar and toss until slightly charred.

title: Thai-Style Green Herb Curry with Vegetables

instructions.text: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Blend the basil, cilantro, chilies, garlic, ginger, and lime juice into a green paste.
Fry the paste in the oil until fragrant.
Add the broth and diced sweet potato and simmer until nearly tender.
Add the zucchini, pepper, and cubed tofu and simmer until tender.
Off the heat, stir in the yogurt and serve over rice.
Simmer the chicken until cooked through, then shred.
Finely shred the cabbage and cut the carrots and pepper into matchsticks.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, honey, and a splash of water.
Toss the vegetables, chicken, and herbs with the dressing.
Fry the sliced garlic in the oil until golden and crisp, then set aside.
Simmer the rice in the broth with the sliced ginger until soft.
Roll the chicken into small balls and drop into the soup to cook.
Season with soy sauce.
Serve topped with fried garlic, green onion, and cilantro.
Blend the lime juice, garlic, cilantro, soy sauce, brown sugar, and pepper into a marinade.
Cut the chicken into pieces and marinate.
Thread onto skewers and grill or broil until charred and cooked through.
Serve with cucumber slices.
Stir-fry the garlic and chilies in the oil until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink, then push aside.
Scramble the eggs, then add the rice, soy sauce, and sugar and stir-fry until hot.
Fold in the basil until wilted.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Pad Pak Ruam (Thai Mixed Vegetable Stir-Fry)

instructions.text: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Cut all the vegetables into bite-size pieces.
Stir-fry the garlic in the oil until fragrant, then add the carrot and broccoli with a splash of water.
Add the cabbage, mushrooms, and pepper and stir-fry until crisp-tender.
Season with soy sauce and sugar and serve over rice.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Salt the salmon and broil or pan-sear until golden and just cooked.
Thinly slice the cucumber and toss with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Soft-boil the eggs.
Blanch the spinach, squeeze dry, and dress with soy sauce.
Serve the salmon with rice, egg, cucumber pickle, and spinach.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Spoon the steaming rice into bowls and make a well in the center.
Crack an egg into each well and add soy sauce.
Whip the egg into the hot rice with chopsticks until fluffy and pale.
Top with green onion and a few drops of sesame oil.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool in cold water, and peel.
Mash the yolks with the yogurt, mustard, sugar, salt, and pepper until creamy.
Finely chop the whites and fold them in.
Butter the bread, fill thickly with the egg salad, and cut off the crusts.
Cut each sandwich in half to serve.
Rinse the rice and simmer it in the broth with the ginger, stirring now and then, until soft and creamy.
Stir in the beaten eggs and cook until just set in ribbons.
Season with soy sauce.
Top with sliced green onion.
Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks with the milk, then whisk in the flour and baking powder.
Beat the whites with the sugar to stiff, glossy peaks.
Gently fold the whites into the yolk batter in three additions.
Pile tall mounds into a buttered nonstick pan over low heat, add a splash of water, and cover.
Carefully flip, add another splash of water, cover, and cook until set.
Serve right away with butter and honey.
Finely shred the cabbage, carrot, and green onion and beat into the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Cook the egg mixture in half the butter as two thick, bread-sized omelettes.
Toast the bread in the remaining butter until golden.
Layer each sandwich with an omelette, a sprinkle of sugar, cheese, and a thin smear of tomato paste.
Simmer the chicken with the garlic and ginger in the broth until cooked, then shred.
Toast the rinsed rice in the sesame oil for a minute.
Add the rice and finely diced carrot to the broth and simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Return the chicken and season with soy sauce.
Top with green onion.
Finely grate the potatoes and onion and drain off the liquid, keeping the starch that settles at the bottom.
Mix the potato with the starch, sliced green onion, and a pinch of salt.
Spoon thin rounds into the hot oil and fry until crisp and golden on both sides.
Serve with soy sauce mixed with rice vinegar.
Whisk the flour with 150 ml water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter.
Spread half the batter thinly in a lightly oiled pan and crack an egg over it, spreading it out.
Scatter with green onion and cilantro and cook until set, then flip.
Stir the tomato paste, honey, and soy sauce into a sauce and brush it on.
Add lettuce, fold into a rectangle, and repeat with the rest.
Beat the eggs with the sliced green onion and a pinch of salt.
Pour half the egg into an oiled pan and immediately lay a tortilla on top.
When the egg sets, flip and toast the tortilla side until golden.
Roll it up, slice into pieces, and repeat.
Serve with soy sauce for dipping.
Rinse the rice and bring it to a boil with 2 l water and the ginger.
Simmer, stirring now and then, until the rice starts to break down.
Add the peeled, cubed sweet potato and simmer until soft and the congee is creamy.
Season lightly with salt, or keep it plain to serve with savory sides.

title: Soy Sauce Fried Eggs over Rice

instructions.text: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Fry the eggs in hot oil until the edges are crisp and lacy.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, and a splash of water, pour into the pan, and spoon over the eggs until glossy.
Serve over rice with sliced green onion.
Brown the chicken in the oil with half the soy sauce.
Divide the chicken between two small pans or ramekins and crack two eggs into each.
Cook covered over low heat until the whites set and the yolks stay runny.
Top with green onion, pepper, and the remaining soy sauce.
Serve with toast for dipping.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Beat the eggs with the raw chicken, soy sauce, and a squeeze of lime until frothy.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot and pour in the egg mixture so it puffs up.
Cook until crisp and golden, flip, and cook until the chicken is done.
Serve over rice.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt, then stir in the milk and knead into a soft dough. Rest, covered.
Roll out thin and cut into small strips. Press two strips together with a chopstick.
Fry in hot oil, turning, until puffed and golden.
Drain and serve warm with honey for dipping.

title: Thai Basil Scrambled Eggs over Rice

instructions.text: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Fry the garlic and chili in the oil until fragrant.
Add the beaten eggs and soy sauce and scramble gently.
Fold in the basil until wilted.
Serve over rice.
Cook the onion, garlic, and jalapeño in the butter until soft.
Add the tomato and cook until soft.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, cover, and cook until the whites are set.
Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt, then add water to make a firm dough. Rest.
Shape into small flat rounds.
Fry in the oil, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Fry or scramble the eggs.
Split the johnny cakes and serve with the eggs.
Fry the diced bacon until crisp.
Add the diced onion, pepper, and tomato and cook until soft.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble gently until just set.
Serve with toasted bread.

title: Jerk-Spiced Sweet Potato Hash with Eggs

instructions.text: Dice the sweet potatoes small and toss with the cinnamon, paprika, pepper, and salt.
Fry in the oil until browned and tender.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until soft.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, cover, and cook until set.
Finish with green onion and lime juice.
Simmer the rice in 480 ml water until it begins to soften.
Add the milk and cinnamon and simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the honey and a pinch of salt.
Serve warm.
Soak the lentils in hot water until soft.
Drain and blend with the ginger, chili, and a little water into a thick, pourable batter. Season with salt and cumin seeds.
Stir in the finely chopped onion and cilantro.
Spread ladlefuls thinly on a hot oiled skillet and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve with yogurt.
Cut the bread into small cubes.
Fry the mustard seeds in the oil until they pop, then add the onion and chili and cook until soft.
Add the tomato and turmeric and cook until soft.
Add the bread and toss until coated and lightly toasted.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash.
Fry the mustard seeds in 1 tsp butter, add the onion, chili, and turmeric, then fold in the potato with salt.
Blend the mint and cilantro with a little water and salt into a green chutney.
Spread the bread with chutney, fill with potato and sliced cucumber and tomato.
Toast the sandwiches in the remaining butter until golden.
Tear the pita into pieces and toast until crisp.
Warm the chickpeas in a little of their liquid with the cumin.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, and salt.
Layer the pita, then the warm chickpeas, then the yogurt sauce.
Toast the almonds in the butter and pour over the top, then add parsley.
Mix the oregano, cumin, and a pinch of salt with 2 tbsp olive oil.
Spread over the pitas and bake at 220°C (425°F) until crisp at the edges.
Season the yogurt with salt and the remaining oil.
Serve the warm pita with the yogurt, sliced cucumber and tomato, and mint.
Season the yogurt with salt, spread on plates, and drizzle with olive oil.
Soft-boil the eggs.
Slice the cucumber and tomato.
Arrange the eggs, vegetables, olives, and mint around the yogurt and serve with warm pita.

title: Greek Yogurt with Honey and Walnuts

instructions.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, then roughly chop.
Spoon the yogurt into bowls.
Drizzle with honey and top with walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon.
Toast the bread until crisp and golden.
Rub each slice with the cut side of a garlic clove.
Halve the tomatoes and grate them, discarding the skins.
Spoon the tomato onto the toast, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Grate the tomatoes and cook them in the olive oil until thick and jammy.
Add the beaten eggs and stir gently until softly set.
Fold in the crumbled feta and oregano.
Serve with toasted bread.

title: Greek Spinach and Feta Egg Muffins

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and oil a 12-cup muffin tin.
Chop the spinach, tomato, and red onion and divide among the cups with the crumbled feta.
Whisk the eggs with the oregano, salt, and pepper and pour over the vegetables.
Bake until puffed and set.
Keep in the fridge for quick breakfasts through the week.
Cook the garlic and pepper flakes in the oil until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and simmer into a thick sauce.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, cover, and cook until the whites are set.
Top with parmesan and basil and serve with crusty bread.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Cook in the oil in a nonstick pan, stirring, until mostly set.
Scatter with diced tomato, mozzarella, and torn basil.
Fold and cook until the cheese melts.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and oil a 12-cup muffin tin.
Grate the zucchini and squeeze out the water.
Whisk the eggs, milk, parmesan, chopped basil, salt, and pepper, then stir in the zucchini.
Divide among the cups and bake until set and golden.

title: Soft Scrambled Eggs on Tomato Bruschetta

instructions.text: Dice the tomatoes and toss with torn basil, olive oil, and salt.
Toast the bread and rub with garlic.
Scramble the eggs slowly in the butter over low heat until creamy.
Top the toasts with the eggs and spoon the tomatoes over.

title: Oeufs en Cocotte (Baked Eggs with Spinach)

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and butter two ramekins.
Wilt the spinach in a pan, squeeze dry, and divide between the ramekins.
Crack two eggs into each, spoon over the cream, and top with parmesan.
Set the ramekins in a dish of hot water and bake until the whites are set.
Serve with toast soldiers.
Finely dice the tomato, onion, and jalapeño — the colors of the Mexican flag.
Cook them in the oil until softened.
Add the beaten eggs and scramble until just set.
Serve with warm tortillas.
Dice the potatoes small and fry in the oil until golden and tender.
Add the onion and chili powder and cook until soft.
Add the beaten eggs and scramble until set.
Fill warm tortillas and top with sliced avocado.
Mash the beans in a pan with a splash of their liquid until thick and spreadable.
Butter the cut rolls, spread with beans, and top with cheese.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) until the cheese melts.
Dice the tomato, onion, and jalapeño with cilantro and salt for pico de gallo.
Top the molletes with pico de gallo.
Cook the bacon until crisp.
Toast the buns in the butter.
Fry the eggs and top with the cheese, covering the pan so it melts.
Build the sandwiches with egg, cheese, and bacon.
Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt and spread on the toast.
Fry the eggs in the oil until the whites set.
Top each toast with an egg and the pepper flakes.
Dice the potatoes and parboil until just tender, then drain.
Fry in the butter until crisp and golden.
Add the onion, pepper, and paprika and cook until soft.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, top with cheese, cover, and cook until set.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Cook and crumble the bacon, and chop the spinach.
Whisk the eggs and milk with salt and pepper.
Divide the bacon, spinach, and cheese among the cups and pour in the eggs.
Bake until puffed and set.
Toast the bread.
Spread with peanut butter.
Drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.
Bring the broth to a boil and add the pasta.
Simmer, stirring often, until tender and most of the broth is absorbed.
Off the heat, quickly stir in the beaten egg so it turns silky without scrambling.
Stir in the butter and parmesan and season with pepper.
